554c01c9451fbb1457a3dbbf64f167d3a47d151b.summary: Red Canary's 2025 Threat Detection Report reviews threats it detected at customers in 2024, about 93,000 confirmed. Topics include ransomware precursors, initial access via fake CAPTCHA paste-and-run lures and fake browser updates, identity attacks, edge-device vulnerabilities such as ScreenConnect and FortiClient EMS, infostealers such as LummaC2 and macOS stealers, VPN abuse, cloud attacks and North Korean IT worker insiders. Top threats include SocGholish, Impacket and Scarlet Goldfinch.

hedges: Red Canary cannot definitively say that suspicious activity it uncovered was associated with DPRK IT workers.
It is difficult to say with certainty whether identity attacks are increasing, steady or decreasing.
Some of the activity shares significant overlaps with activity tracked by Microsoft as Storm-0844.
Mandiant believes the DPRK insider campaign may date back as far as 2018.
Red Canary assesses Amber Albatross as nefarious based on suspicious reconnaissance and heavy obfuscation, and has yet to discern how the malware uses the data it collects.
The report excludes unwanted software and confirmed testing from its data, consistent with past years.
